multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which counts unique learners rather than enrolments?

div.p: COUNT(learner_id) counts non-null enrolments; only DISTINCT collapses the repeats to unique learners.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: You want only groups whose total exceeds 100. You use:

div.p: WHERE runs before grouping, so it cannot see an aggregate. HAVING is the filter for grouped results.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: After joining two tables you notice the row count is far higher than either input. The most likely cause is:

choice.div: A many-to-many match on the join key, multiplying rows.
The database is returning duplicates at random.

div.p: If the join key is not unique on one side, each match multiplies. Check the grain before and after, and aggregate one side first where appropriate.
